verses.text: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head on his bed: then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters.
Daniel spoke and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea.
Four great animals came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings: I saw until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made to stand on two feet as a man; and a man’s heart was given to it.
Behold, another animal, a second, like a bear; and it was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth: and they said thus to it, Arise, devour much flesh.
After this I saw, and behold, another, like a leopard, which had on its back four wings of a bird; the animal had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.

After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, a fourth animal, awesome and powerful, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet: and it was diverse from all the animals that were before it; and it had ten horns.

I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.

I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
A fiery stream issued and came out from before him: thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
I saw at that time because of the voice of the great words which the horn spoke; I saw even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
As for the rest of the animals, their dominion was taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.

There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved within my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.
I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
These great animals, which are four, are four kings, who shall arise out of the earth.
But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.

Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was diverse from all of them, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of brass; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them;
until the ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.
Thus he said, The fourth animal shall be a fourth kingdom on earth, which shall be diverse from all the kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.
As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom shall ten kings arise: and another shall arise after them; and he shall be diverse from the former, and he shall put down three kings.

He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High; and he shall think to change the times and the law; and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
But the judgment shall be set, and they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it to the end.

The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts much troubled me, and my face was changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.

footnotes.content: Notice how Daniel *records* what he's been given to see—he doesn't hoard it or doubt it. When God shows us something true, the faithful response is to witness it, write it down, and share the weight of it. The Lord honors honest attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sea often stirs with trouble and chaos in Scripture. Daniel doesn't hide from what he sees—he faces it squarely in his vision. Sometimes the Holy Spirit draws near to us precisely in the places where our hearts feel most unsettled.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four beasts, each unlike the others. The kingdoms of man are restless, grasping, unpredictable—but they rise and fall while the throne of God stands firm. What seems terrible and unstoppable in our day is already measured and numbered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A lion with eagle's wings—strength and speed combined—until its wings are plucked away and it stands on human feet, given a human heart. Power without wisdom, without compassion, does not last. The Lord knows how to humble the proud.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A bear raised up on one side, ribs in its mouth, commanded to devour. Unbalanced and ravenous—the appetite of kingdoms that consume everything. Yet even this dreadful beast has an appointed end; it does not reign forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leopard swift and cunning, with four wings and four heads—multiplied authority and swiftness. Dominion is given to it, but given *by God*, not stolen. Remember this when you see earthly power striding: its bounds were set before the world began.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A fourth beast—awesome, powerful, exceedingly strong, iron teeth, ten horns. More terrible than the rest. When you see evil reaching its crescendo, rising to a height that seems unstoppable, hold fast: this very vision is God's way of saying He sees it all and has the final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A little horn arises, eyes like a man's, a mouth speaking great things. Pride and self-exaltation wear many faces across history. But notice: Daniel sees it. The watchful eye of faith recognizes boasting when it rises, and knows it will not stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ancient of Days takes His throne—white as snow, hair like wool, throne of flaming fire. This is the God who dwells in unapproachable light, and He shows Himself here not to terrify but to reign. Compare this throne to the thrones of the beasts below: His alone is eternal, holy, and just.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten thousand times ten thousand serve Him—multitudes beyond counting. A fiery stream issues before Him; the judgment is set; books are opened. The counsel of the Almighty is not hurried or confused, but deliberate and complete. Nothing escapes His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because of the great words the horn speaks, Daniel watches until the fourth beast is slain, its body destroyed and burned. Pride that lifts itself against the Most High is heard, recorded, and answered. The arc of history turns on God's judgment, not on human schemes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rest of the animals lose their dominion, yet their lives are prolonged for a season and a time. Even in judgment, there is mercy and measure. The Lord does not waste or act in haste; He accomplishes His purposes with perfect justice and perfect timing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One like the Son of Man comes with the clouds and approaches the Ancient of Days. This is the figure Daniel sees, and it speaks across centuries to every heart that knows Jesus as Lord. He is coming, and His kingdom shall not be moved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To Him is given dominion, glory, and a kingdom—everlasting, never to pass away. All peoples and nations shall serve Him. When earthly crowns fall and thrones crumble, His throne remains. Our hope rests not on what we can see and control, but on His unshakeable reign.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel's spirit is grieved, his visions troubled him. A true encounter with God's majesty and judgment does not leave us untouched. Reverent fear and sorrow over evil's reality are the marks of a heart attuned to God's holiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel approaches one standing by—likely an angel—and asks for truth. He doesn't assume; he asks. Wisdom begins when we acknowledge that we need the help of others to understand God's mind, and that asking is not weakness but obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The four great animals are four kings who shall arise. Kingdoms come and go; men rise to power only for a season. But God's kingdom is not counted among the beasts. It is eternal and belongs to His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess it forever and ever. This is the promise beneath the whole vision: God's people, though they may suffer and be shaken in this age, shall inherit the kingdom that cannot be shaken. Hold to this with both hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel presses deeper—he wants to understand the fourth beast in all its terror: iron teeth, brass nails, devouring and trampling. Sometimes faith means facing the hardness of evil squarely, not turning away. Knowledge of God's power grows when we see evil's reality without denial.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ten horns, the other horn that rose up, the eyes and boastful mouth—fiercer in look than its fellows. Ambition and pride clothe themselves in many garments. But the searching gaze of faith sees through the costume to the emptiness beneath.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The horn makes war with the saints and prevails against them. Yes, the saints suffer. This is not hidden from God's knowledge or contrary to His purposes; it is written beforehand. Our suffering is not meaningless, but measured and bound by His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Until the Ancient of Days comes—then judgment is given to the saints, and they possess the kingdom. The promise is not that the saints will escape suffering, but that they will be vindicated and exalted at last. This is the anchor for every faithful heart in hard times.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fourth kingdom shall devour the whole earth, tread it down, and break it in pieces. Such is the nature of human empires apart from God—they consume, they crush. Yet the interpreter reveals this not to terrify but to make clear what lies hidden in the machinery of earthly power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten kings arise from this kingdom; another comes after, diverse from the rest, and puts down three. Power shifts and struggles among the kingdoms of men—they jostle, they devour one another. But none of this is a surprise to Him who sits on the throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This king speaks against the Most High, wears out the saints, thinks to change times and law—the height of rebel pride. But he is given into God's hand only for *a time and times and half a time*—not forever, not even long. The Lord has set the boundary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The judgment shall be set, and his dominion shall be consumed and destroyed to the end. This is the sentence pronounced on all that rises against the living God. Let those who trust in Jesus know: the final word belongs to Him, and it is a word of justice and peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The kingdom and dominion shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High—an everlasting kingdom. All dominions shall serve and obey Him. This is the crown jewel of the vision: not just God's judgment on evil, but the eternal honor and joy given to His faithful people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel's thoughts trouble him and his face changes, yet he keeps the matter in his heart. Readers today hear an echo in this: when God draws near and shows us His glory and His justice, we are changed forever. We carry the weight of what we've seen, and we hold it close—not to keep it secret, but to let it reshape us in silence and reverence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
